sections.h2: Where is the Ross County Recorder's office?
sections.html:
You will find the office in the courthouse, 2 North Paint Street, Suite E, Chillicothe, Ohio 45601. Its number is 740-702-3000. Documents sent by mail go to PO Box 6162, Chillicothe, OH 45601, and the office email is rossrec@bright.net. The treasurer's office is next door in Suite F, so a tax balance and a recording can be handled in one trip.

The county has a long paper trail. The county dates to August 20, 1798, and its seat, Chillicothe, served as Ohio's first and third capital. Nineteenth-century surveyors described almost one hundred earthwork enclosures and five hundred mounds in the county, and Hopewell Culture National Historical Park and Adena State Memorial are among its protected sites. Modern deeds sit on top of more than two centuries of recorded transfers.

sections.h2: What is the price of recording a deed in Ross County?
sections.html:
The fee sheet, dated January 1, 2025, prices a document by its page count. A one or two page document is $39.00, a three page one is $47.00, and every added page is another $8.00. Documents that fall outside the standard format under section 317.114 carry a $20.00 surcharge, and each marginal reference adds $4.00. The office states that its recording fees are set by the Ohio Legislature.

Source: Ross County Recorder Table of Fees. The schedule continues to 88 pages at $727.00 and then adds $8.00 for each page beyond that.

State law explains the structure. The state fee statute sets the pattern: a base fee plus an equal housing trust fund fee, with an optional preservation surcharge of up to five dollars (section 317.32). A postage-paid, self-addressed envelope is required with every filing, so include one when you mail a deed.

sections.h2: What other recorder charges should a Ross County seller know about?
sections.html:
• A certified copy runs $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for every page after it.
  • Ordinary copies are $2.00 per printed page, and the sheet gives $7 for a two-page document and $9 for three pages.
  • Fax charges are $2.00 a page to a local or toll-free number and $4.00 a page to a toll number.
  • According to the recorder, no one needs the original recorded deed to sell or borrow, because a certified copy from the office serves equally well.

These are the office's own figures, and they apply to documents the office handles after a sale, such as copying a recorded deed for a title company or an heir.

sections.h2: How do I search Ross County records online, and what should I avoid?
sections.html:
The recorder's website says most records go back to January 1, 1974 and further, and can be viewed and downloaded free from home through the county's CountyFusion search. The office also assists people in person while they wait. Anyone can see a deed, mortgage or release this way before listing a house.

The office warns about private companies that mail letters or turn up in online searches charging $79.99 to $99.99 for copies of a deed. These companies are not government offices, and the same records are free to view at the courthouse offices. The recorder calls those offers a scam for money, and recommends skipping them. One exception applies to military discharge papers: a DD214 is not a full public record, and only the veteran, a veterans' service office or a funeral director handling burial services can get an unredacted certified copy, free of charge.

sections.h2: What must happen before a Ross County deed reaches the recorder?
sections.html:
Start with signing and acknowledgment. Section 5301.01 names who may take the acknowledgment, including a notary public, judge, court clerk, county auditor, county engineer or mayor. The auditor comes next. After the buyer files a value statement under section 319.202, the Ross County Auditor endorses the deed. It also asks whether the seller's taxes had been cut by a program such as homestead, and whether the land sat in the farm valuation program, which can carry a recoupment charge.

Before the deed goes across the hall, the seller pays the auditor the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax. Section 322.02 lets a county set that transfer tax as high as thirty cents per hundred dollars of value. The Ross County Auditor knows the figure that applies.

sections.h2: How does Ross County property tax fit into a deed closing?
sections.html:
Ross County collects real estate tax one year behind. Per the treasurer, taxes attach to the property and not to its owner, so a new buyer can receive a bill soon after purchase, and the closing papers normally credit the buyer with the prorated share. In 2026 the two installments fell due February 20 and August 21; the treasurer can supply 2027 dates. Get the balance in writing and hand it to the title company.

If back taxes are owed, the treasurer's Delinquent Tax Contract splits them into five equal installments, and the SMART Payments Program spreads them over 30 months or longer. A seller with a contract open should confirm what balance stays with the property. The treasurer applies a 5% late charge when payment is received within ten days and 10% after that.

sections.h2: What if an old family deed in Ross County lacks two witnesses?
sections.html: Ohio treats most such deeds as valid. For an instrument signed before February 1, 2002 and never witnessed by two people as the earlier statute asked, section 5301.01(B) presumes it properly executed unless fraud produced the signature. Once the deed is filed with the recorder, later buyers and lenders have notice of it. Heirs in Ross County who find a mid-century deed in a drawer should still check that it was actually recorded, because the index at the recorder's office is what a title company searches.

sections.h2: What does the Ross County housing stock look like?
sections.html:
Census figures show 76,429 residents and 32,165 housing units, and owners occupy 69.6% of homes. Median home value among owners is $171,500. Owner costs are $1,304 a month with a mortgage and $487 without. Building permits numbered 59 in 2025, and 87.9% of residents had stayed put for a year.

The county holds one city, Chillicothe, villages from Adelphi to South Salem, and 16 townships. Ohio University has run a campus in Chillicothe since 1966. Seven counties border Ross (Fayette, Pickaway, Hocking, Vinton, Jackson, Pike and Highland), and a farm that straddles a county line has its deed recorded wherever each piece of land lies. The terrain is frequent wooded hills with farmland between them, so any sale of acreage should be checked with the auditor for farm valuation before the deed is signed.

faqs.q: What does a short deed cost to record in Ross County?
faqs.a: $39.00 under the fee sheet that took effect January 1, 2025. Pages past the second add $8.00 each, and non-standard documents add $20.00.

faqs.q: What address takes a mailed Ross County deed?
faqs.a: Send it to PO Box 6162, Chillicothe, OH 45601, with payment and the postage-paid return envelope the office requires on every filing.

faqs.q: Can I view Ross County records without paying a service?
faqs.a: Yes. Most records back to January 1, 1974 can be viewed and downloaded free through the county's CountyFusion site. Copies made in the office are $2.00 per printed page on the fee sheet.

faqs.q: Must I hold the original deed to sell in Ross County?
faqs.a: No. No. A certified copy from the recorder is as good as the original for a sale or a mortgage. Page one of a certified copy is $5.00, and later pages are $2.00 each.

faqs.q: Which office endorses a Ross County deed before recording?
faqs.a: The County Auditor does, after the buyer files a statement of value. The seller settles the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax with the auditor first.
